newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: National Mutual to offer 448 mln shares.
newsitem.headline: National Mutual to offer 448 mln shares.

text.p: Australian life office National Mutual Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it would offer 448 million shares at a retail price of A$1.50 per share as part of its plan to demutualise and list on the Australian Stock Exchange.
National Mutual, 51 percent owned by French insurer AXA SA, said institutions would be offered a minimum of 280 million shares at an indicative price range of between A$1.35 and A$1.55 per share.
National Mutual said policy holders took 55 percent of the total 701 million shares they were entitled to.

"Eligible policy holders have accepted more than 384 million shares," the group said in a statement, adding that another 80 million shares from the retail portion of the float had been reserved for preferential allocation to policyholders.
The retail portion of the offer comprises 168 million shares and closes on September 27.
The institutional offer will be open from October 2 to 4, and National Mutual plans to list on the Australian Stock Exchange on October 8.

"The public sale price (the final price) will be determined after the close of the institutional offer and set at the lower of the retail application price and the institutional sale price," National Mutual said.
"This will be announced on October 7. If the public sale price is lower than A$1.50...successful retail applicants will receive a refund," it said.

National Mutual should get a strong response from institutional investors, given the high take up of shares by existing policy holders, said J.B. Were and Son group managing director Terrence Campbell told reporters after announcement.

"We are starting something new in the market because it (a life office) is a new sector but it does look as though its going to be reflected in demand," said Campbell, whose firm is joint manager for the issue with McIntosh Corporate Ltd.
"We expect strong overseas institutional demand," he said.
